posts.title: I Closed Two Reverse-Engineering Projects on Measurement. Much of What I Concluded Along the Way Was My Instrument Talking
posts.description: Two campaigns to run a mobile app's anti-abuse library on a laptop both ended without the goal. What I kept was a method: every instrument needs a positive control, a null return is not a refusal, and a retraction ledger with a checker that fails when a correction goes unindexed.

posts.title: I Raised My Crawler's Concurrency After It Passed Its Own Gate. By Morning It Was Slower Than Before, and the Experiment Had Grown the Backlog
posts.description: I wrote a runbook with explicit RAISE and LOWER rules, raised a worker's concurrency from 8 to 12 only after all five gate conditions passed, and read +53% at 15 minutes. By the next morning the breaker was cycling, throughput had collapsed below the old baseline, and the backlog was 115 thousand larger.

posts.title: I Read a 429 as a Quota, Then as Google Play Integrity. It Was the User-Agent My HTTP Library Filled In
posts.description: A mobile API answered every correctly signed request with a generic 429. I blamed a per-key quota, then wrote up Play Integrity attestation as a wall I couldn't get over. One header diff showed it was the User-Agent, which my library had been filling in with its own name. Then I counted how many other places do the same.
